# 100.00 USD arrives in the USD bank and is parked against a CAD account.
#
# Q-039, on the book fx_usd_invoice_cad_income.txt builds: INV-USD-001 is
# 100.00 USD, its receivable is USD, and this is the money paying it.
#
# Nobody knew that yet when it was booked, so the other side is
# `Assets:Due From Director`, which is CAD. GnuCash has to quote the entry in a
# currency both sides can be expressed in, so the transaction is CAD and the
# `Assets:Due From Director` split carries 139.00 of it at 1.39.
#
# **Neither figure is a fact about the settlement.** The invoice is USD, the
# receivable is USD, the bank is USD: 100 USD arrived against 100 USD owed and
# nothing converts. Both numbers are an artefact of `Assets:Due From Director`
# being CAD, and both go when it is replaced.
#
# The transaction and its splits state their own guids so a `payment:` block in
# another fixture can name them, rather than a test reading them out of the
# book and building the ledger in Python.
#
# What this fixture produces: one CAD-quoted transaction, in no lot, whose
# other side is the CAD account.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
2026-02-25 * "Money in"
	guid: "c9f27c2b2f324117aa17c7c1f48fbafd"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.00 USD
		guid: "1a2b3c4d5e6f70819a2b3c4d5e6f7081"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.39"
		value: "139.00"
	Assets:Due From Director -139.00 CAD
		guid: "614b338df4f94c359aa35ffacc2dadcf"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-139.00"
